title: The Inner Work (Teaching Simplified for Back to School Series)
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Kicking off his August 2022 back-to-school Teaching Simplified series, Dave Stuart Jr. compiles the week's threads into a single "inner work of the teacher" post. He walks readers through the Everest exercise (naming a course's purpose in one sentence), a "lumpy growth" prompt for choosing one professional-growth focus, a time-management technique for visualizing hard boundaries on work hours, and a cognitive-reframing tool for swapping unhelpful, comparative self-talk for abundance-based alternatives. The piece frames all four as facets of one underlying skill: the inner, often-neglected work teachers must do on themselves before the school year starts. Real examples from music, art, agricultural science, and Spanish teachers illustrate the Everest exercise in practice.
points: Frames "the inner work of teaching" as a distinct skill/muscle with three components introduced that week: focusing intentions (Everest sentence), pursuing lumpy (single-focus) growth, and setting boundaried work hours.

The "Everest" exercise — boiling a course's purpose down to one sentence — forces teachers to articulate a north-star answer before the year starts, illustrated with real examples from music, art, ag science, and Spanish teachers.
Recommends visualizing literal time boundaries (a fixed weekday stop time, a capped Saturday morning) and sharing them with an accountability partner, rather than just deciding on limits mentally.

The "unhelpful thing vs. helpful alternative" reframing technique swaps comparative, all-or-nothing self-talk ("I must be the best," "I can't fail") for abundance-based, growth-oriented language, applied by writing the helpful version on an index card taped to the monitor.
quotes: The essential question that this article's sections seek to answer for you and me is this: What methods are best suited to getting our heads and hearts right for a new school year?
